name: Nawab Shafiq
role: Pakistani Prime Minister equivalent — political authority during IC-814 era
real_life_inspiration: Nawaz Sharif — Prime Minister of Pakistan during the IC-814 hijacking (December 1999). The Kargil War (May–July 1999) had just ended; Sharif was removed in a military coup by General Pervez Musharraf on 12 October 1999 — barely two months before the IC-814 hijacking. The film's Nawab Shafiq captures this politically weakened Pakistani PM who is simultaneously managing post-Kargil fallout and military pressure.

inspiration_notes.nawaz_sharif_parallel: Nawaz Sharif was PM during Kargil (which he reportedly wasn't fully briefed on by the army before it started — a documented civil-military fracture). He was ousted October 1999. IC-814 happened December 1999 — by then Musharraf's military government was in charge. The film likely compresses the timeline.
inspiration_notes.kargil_context: The 1999 Kargil War's civil-military breakdown in Pakistan — where the army launched the operation without full PM knowledge — is the subtext behind Nawab Shafiq's political weakness. He is the nominal authority; the real power is the army (Bade Sahab).
inspiration_notes.film_function: Nawab Shafiq represents the Pakistani civilian political class that has nominal authority but is fundamentally subordinate to the military in matters of India-Pakistan operations. He is the face that Devavrat Kapoor negotiates with; the army is the actual power behind the hijacking.
inspiration_notes.oracle_note: Like Zarwari, Nawab Shafiq is non-operational. He is the civilian political layer above which Bade Sahab operates. Relevant for the Stackelberg hierarchy as: Bade Sahab (COAS) → Nawab Shafiq (PM, subordinate) → Jameel Jamali (politician) → Rehman Dakait (criminal) → operations.
